headline: Highest risk is data leakage from Airbyte’s broad egress into a non-egress scheduling agent; other pairwise risks are limited by the second agent’s lack of write/network surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, and both profiles are non-runnable with no filesystem or MCP bridge. The only plausible pathway is manual copy-paste of Airbyte outputs into awesome-python workflows, which is an unusual configuration and small blast radius. Because neither profile proves a parser boundary, uncertainty stays low rather than none.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Airbyte-generated text into awesome-python inputs
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added between the two agents
mitigations: Avoid copy-pasting untrusted Airbyte output into downstream prompts
Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable any shared clipboard sync
Add a human review step before reuse of generated text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte has broad network egress and touches business data, so it can transmit sensitive workspace content outward. awesome-python has no network egress and no data classes touched, so it is not itself a leak source, but the pair still creates a one-way exposure path if Airbyte ingests data that should remain local. The interaction is inferred from profiles, not directly observed.
conditions: IF Airbyte is connected to business data that must remain local
IF Airbyte sends that data to external services during normal operation
mitigations: Restrict Airbyte connectors to approved sources
Route sensitive datasets through a redaction step first
Disable unnecessary outbound destinations
Review Airbyte destination settings before sync

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write surface is documented. Airbyte exposes API calls and broad egress, while awesome-python has no I/O surfaces, no network egress, and no write permissions. Without a shared mutable resource, there is no plausible capability conflict pathway in the pair.
conditions: IF a shared writable directory or database is introduced for both agents
IF both agents are granted write access to the same mutable resource
mitigations: Keep write scopes disjoint
Do not mount a shared writable workspace
Use separate service accounts
Add locking if a shared resource is later introduced

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce data outputs, but awesome-python is a static collection repo with no runnable action surface or downstream authority documented. That makes an automated cascade unlikely; the main risk is a human or external orchestrator treating Airbyte output as authoritative and reusing it elsewhere. Because the second agent lacks action-taking capability, blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF Airbyte output is manually treated as authoritative by a downstream process
IF awesome-python content is repurposed into an action-taking workflow
mitigations: Require verification before reusing Airbyte outputs
Label generated data as untrusted
Keep awesome-python as reference-only
Add a checksum or review gate before downstream use

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad egress, so residency or retention issues are possible if it is pointed at regulated datasets. awesome-python touches no data and has no egress, so it does not add a separate compliance burden. The pair’s compliance risk is therefore mostly Airbyte-specific and depends on how it is configured.
conditions: IF Airbyte processes regulated business data under a residency or retention policy
IF outbound transfers from Airbyte are not covered by the operator’s compliance controls
mitigations: Confirm data residency requirements for Airbyte destinations
Limit Airbyte to non-regulated datasets
Review retention settings before enabling sync
Document the lawful basis for each data source
